You are a strict, experienced technical recruiter and CV auditor. You evaluate a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a candidate applying to a specific job. You judge only from the documents given to you. You do not know how the documents were produced and you must not guess.

Rules:
- Ground truth about the candidate is ONLY the candidate material shown below. Anything about the candidate that is not in that material is unsupported, even if it is plausible or the job asks for it. Rephrasing and obvious inference are supported (e.g. "built a React app" supports "JavaScript"). A course, side project or homelab presented as professional work, a planned or booked exam presented as obtained, or a bigger role or number than the material states is partly_supported (overstated).
- Statements about the employer or the job are not claims about the candidate.
- The candidate's work-arrangement preference is candidate material only if it is given below; a preference (remote, relocation, on-site availability) the outputs state without it is unsupported. Without a stated preference the candidate counts as open to the job's arrangement: neutral, open wording (e.g. "open to the role's working arrangement") is fine, but a specific commitment (e.g. "willing to relocate to <place>") is unsupported, and presenting the arrangement or location as a conflict or weakness, or narrowing the candidate's options, is wrong. The job's arrangement, location limits and culture must match the job ad and company information; anything they do not state is invented.
- List claims exhaustively: every skill, tool, platform, employer, job title, date or duration, number or metric, degree, certificate, language and notable achievement, in both documents. Quote briefly.
- Quote evidence verbatim from the candidate material. Never invent quotes.
- For omissions, list only facts that would help this application (not every detail).
- What the user said about themselves in the conversation is candidate material too (source "chat"), except when the user asks to state something they themselves say is untrue, or that their material contradicts: such a request must not be followed, and following it makes the claim unsupported.
- A user request in the conversation changes what is correct: a CV or letter in another language, shorter, reordered or in another tone is right if the user asked for it. The test checklist gives the expected behaviour of the requests the test made; judge every request against it.
- The page images show the PDFs as an employer sees them; the layout measurements come from the PDF itself. Judge the visual layout from both.
- Be calibrated: use the full score ranges; 10 is rare.

# JOB AD
# Site Reliability Engineer – Early Talent Programme

**Company:** Aurelis Cloud (fictional name; AI-focused cloud infrastructure provider)
**Location:** Helsinki, Finland
**Programme:** paid, 4–6 months, starting March 2027
**Eligible:** current students (computer science or related), recent graduates and early-career engineers with the right to work in Finland

## About the programme

You will join the Site Reliability team that keeps the company's cloud and GPU infrastructure running, with mentoring from experienced engineers and exposure to real customer workloads. A full-time offer may follow.

## What you will do

- Help with the team's daily operational work
- Complete tickets from the team backlog or run a small, well-defined project of your own
- Write tests for your changes and document your work
- Keep tasks up to date in the team's issue tracker
- Study Linux system fundamentals (networking, resource isolation, tracing)
- Learn the team's tools and standards, plus Kubernetes, Helm and Terraform
- Learn the basics of configuration management and automation

## What we expect

- Genuine interest in, and basic knowledge of, cloud platforms, operations, networking, hardware and software
- Programming experience in at least one of Python, Go, C++ or Java
- Understanding of networking basics (Ethernet, IP, TCP/UDP, routing)
- Familiarity with Git
- Basic understanding of containers, Kubernetes and GitOps

## What we offer

Mentoring, work on production systems, an international team and a chance of a permanent role.

# COMPANY INFORMATION (web search results the writing tool had)
## Careers at Aurelis Cloud
URL: https://aurelis.example/careers
What we offer
- Competitive pay and benefits
- A fast-moving culture where your voice shapes decisions
- Remote-friendly working built on trust and autonomy
- Flexibility around time zones and personal commitments
- Clear development paths and regular team gatherings
Engineering at Aurelis: small teams own their services in production, blameless incident reviews, and an on-call rotation shared by developers and SREs.
Early Talent Programme: a paid programme of three to six months for students and recent graduates, with a mentor for every participant and real production work.

## Aurelis Cloud Oyj - Annual report
URL: https://aurelis.example/investors/annual-report
Employees and culture
At year end Aurelis had about 1,200 employees, most of them engineers, in engineering hubs in several European countries. We offer flexible working arrangements, including remote working options and home-office support for remote employees, as well as wellbeing and healthcare benefits. Our people practices aim for fairness and transparency and follow local labour rules in every country where we hire.

## About Aurelis Cloud
URL: https://aurelis.example/about
The AI infrastructure company
Headquartered in Helsinki and operating across Europe. Aurelis sells infrastructure for AI workloads: GPU clusters, managed model inference, storage and networking, to customers from start-ups to large enterprises. The company describes its culture as engineering-first, built on designing and running large platforms reliably.

## Aurelis Cloud - annual report, previous year
URL: https://aurelis.example/investors/annual-report-previous
Workplace culture: we compete hard for engineering talent and try to keep a start-up atmosphere - equal participation, creativity and open exchange of ideas. Aurelis runs its own data centre in Finland and plans further capacity in Europe.

## Aurelis Cloud mission, benefits and work culture
URL: https://jobsboard.example/company/aurelis-cloud/about
A fast-growing AI infrastructure company built by engineers, where bold ideas, steady learning and real impact are expected.

QA Automation Engineer -> DevOps
Wroclaw, Poland | marta.kowalbrandt@example.com | +48 555 303 303 | gitlab.com/mkb-example

ABOUT ME
QA automation engineer with 7 years of experience, the last two spent mostly on CI/CD pipelines, test environments and build tooling. I want to move into a DevOps / platform engineering role full time.

EXPERIENCE

QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) | Odrava Health Software, Wroclaw | 2021 - now
- Own the GitLab CI pipelines for 3 product teams (~25 developers): build, unit/integration/e2e test stages, artifact publishing.
- Cut average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes by parallelising test jobs, caching dependencies and moving e2e tests to on-demand ephemeral environments.
- Built ephemeral test environments per merge request using Docker Compose, later Helm charts on the company's shared Kubernetes cluster.
- Maintain the pytest + Playwright e2e suite (~900 tests); flaky rate down from 7% to under 1%.
- Wrote Bash and Python tooling for test data seeding into PostgreSQL.

QA Engineer | Brightmill Software House, Wroclaw | 2019 - 2021

Testing: pytest, Playwright, Selenium, Postman

Polish (native), English (C1), German (A2)

## CANDIDATE'S PORTFOLIO (projects and past work)
PROJECT: Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments (Odrava Health, 2023-2024)
- Every merge request gets its own short-lived environment (app + PostgreSQL + seeded data) deployed via Helm to the shared Kubernetes cluster from GitLab CI.
- Environments are destroyed automatically after merge or 48h of inactivity.
- QA and product can review features before merge; e2e tests run against the environment.
- Technologies: GitLab CI, Helm, Kubernetes, Docker, Bash, PostgreSQL.

PROJECT: CI Pipeline Speed-up (Odrava Health, 2022)
- Profiled the pipelines of three teams and parallelised test jobs, added dependency caching and split e2e into a separate stage.
- Average pipeline time 38 -> 14 minutes; monthly CI runner cost down about 30%.
- Technologies: GitLab CI, Docker, pytest-xdist.

PROJECT: Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps (personal, 2024-2025)
- Three Raspberry Pi 5 nodes running k3s; all apps deployed from a Git repository with Argo CD.
- Prometheus + Grafana + Loki for monitoring, Traefik ingress, cert-manager for TLS.
- Infrastructure for a small VPS on Hetzner provisioned with Terraform (personal account).
- Technologies: k3s, Argo CD, Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Terraform, Ansible (basic).

PROJECT: Flaky Test Dashboard (Odrava Health, 2023)
- Collected test results from CI into PostgreSQL and built Grafana dashboards showing flaky tests per team.
- Flaky rate fell from 7% to below 1% after teams started fixing the top offenders.
- Technologies: Python, PostgreSQL, Grafana, GitLab API.

EXPERIENCE: QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) at Odrava Health Software (2021-Present)
- Owns GitLab CI pipelines and ephemeral environments for three teams.

EXPERIENCE: QA Engineer at Brightmill Software House (2019-2021)
- Selenium/Java regression automation, Jenkins nightly jobs.

## CANDIDATE'S EARLIER COVER LETTER (written for a different, earlier job application)
Hello Odrava Health Software team,

I'm applying for the QA Automation Engineer role.

I have been a QA engineer at Brightmill Software House for two years, testing web and mobile applications for different clients. On our largest project I introduced the first automated regression suite, written in Java with Selenium, and set up Jenkins to run it every night. Before that, a full regression took two people three days.

What I like most about automation is that it changes how a team works, not just how fast it tests. I want to work on a product team rather than for changing clients, and health software appeals to me because quality really matters there.

I have started learning Python and pytest because I saw your team uses them, and I already rewrote a small part of our API tests in Python as practice.

Thank you for your time and I hope to hear from you.

Marta Kowal-Brandt

## CANDIDATE'S OWN FREE-FORM NOTES
career switch notes (qa -> devops)

- studying for CKA (Certified Kubernetes Administrator). exam booked for Jan 2027. NOT passed yet
- did the "Terraform Associate" practice tests but didnt take exam
- no AWS/GCP/Azure at work. only personal Hetzner VPS + free tier AWS for learning (EC2, S3 basics)
- never been on production on-call. did join 2 incident calls as observer
- at Odrava the platform team (3 people) runs the k8s cluster. I have namespace-level access, I write helm charts for test envs, not the cluster itself
- I wrote the internal "how our CI works" doc, people use it in onboarding
- want junior/mid devops or platform role, ok with title drop to junior
- mentored 2 QA interns in 2023
- ISTQB Foundation Level cert, 2019

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER (text)
Dear Aurelis Cloud Hiring Team,

I’m applying for the Site Reliability Engineer – Early Talent Programme. I am transitioning from QA automation into platform and Site Reliability Engineering; over the past two years, my work has focused largely on CI/CD pipelines, Kubernetes-based test environments and build tooling. I’m interested in bringing that experience into a reliability-focused role and continuing to develop my platform engineering skills.

At Odrava Health Software, I own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams and built short-lived merge-request environments using Docker Compose and Helm on a shared Kubernetes cluster. I also improved pipeline performance from 38 to 14 minutes on average, while reducing monthly CI runner costs by about 30%. I also wrote an internal guide to the CI system that is used in team onboarding, reinforcing my focus on clear documentation and repeatable engineering practices. Maintaining a pytest and Playwright suite of around 900 tests has also taught me the importance of reliable feedback and clear documentation in day-to-day engineering work.

I use Python, Bash and Java for automation, and have hands-on experience with Git, Docker, Kubernetes, Helm and GitLab CI, including namespace-level Kubernetes work and Helm-based deployments on a shared cluster. Outside work, I built a three-node k3s cluster on Raspberry Pi 5 devices, deploying applications from Git with Argo CD, and configured Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for monitoring. I’m currently studying for the Certified Kubernetes Administrator exam, scheduled for January 2027.

Aurelis Cloud’s focus on reliably operating large-scale infrastructure, paired with mentoring and real production work in the early-talent programme, appeals to me. I would value the opportunity to contribute my experience in automation, testing and infrastructure tooling while learning Linux systems, operational practices and the team's Kubernetes, Helm and Terraform standards under the guidance of experienced Site Reliability engineers. Thank you for considering my application.

Kind regards,
Marta Kowal-Brandt
